learning_activity_name: Describe the fundamentals of reading and writing music based on ABRSM Music Theory Grade V (Rhythm, scales and key signatures, and melody and harmony)
sla_name: Music theory: rhythm, scales and melody (Grade V)
sla_method: ICT- based learning and Case Study
sla_assessment_criteria: Fundamentals of reading and writing music based on ABRSM Music Theory Grade V are described correctly.
sla_teaching_aids: ABRSM music theory guideline|Music scores|Music sheets|Piano|Guitar|Ngoma
sla_references: TET(2023), MUSIC SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: ABRSM Grade V theory builds a solid foundation in rhythm, scales, key signatures, melody and basic harmony that advanced learners need to read and write music accurately.
sla_notes_details: Rhythm at this level covers simple and compound time signatures (2/4, 3/4, 4/4, 6/8, 9/8, 12/8), note and rest values including dotted notes, ties and simple triplets, and grouping notes correctly within a bar. Scales and key signatures cover all major scales and the three forms of minor scales (natural, harmonic, melodic) up to four sharps and four flats, together with the circle of fifths and relative major/minor pairs. Melody and harmony cover phrase structure, cadence types (perfect, plagal, imperfect, interrupted), and simple harmonisation of a melody using the primary triads I, IV and V in root position.
sla_notes_illustrations: Given the key of D major (two sharps, F# and C#), a student writes an eight-bar melody in 4/4 time ending on the tonic D with a perfect cadence (V-I) in the last two bars.
sla_notes_daily_life: Choir leaders and school band directors use these same skills every week to write out parts and check that a hymn or anthem is notated correctly before rehearsal.
sla_exercise: Name the two sharps in the key signature of D major.::F sharp and C sharp.||What is a perfect cadence?::A chord progression from chord V to chord I that gives a strong sense of ending.||Give one difference between a harmonic minor scale and a melodic minor scale.::The harmonic minor raises only the 7th degree going up and down, while the melodic minor raises the 6th and 7th going up but uses the natural minor coming down.

learning_activity_name: Describe theories related to the origins of different music traditions in East Africa
sla_name: Origins of East African music traditions
sla_assessment_criteria: Theories related to origins of music traditions in East Africa are described correctly.
sla_teaching_aids: Audio|Video clips of various East African traditional ensemble performances
sla_references: TET(2023), MUSIC SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Scholars explain the origin of East African music traditions using several theories, including diffusion through migration and trade, and the functional role music played in ritual and work.
sla_notes_details: The diffusionist theory holds that musical styles and instruments spread as Bantu, Nilotic and Cushitic peoples migrated and traded across East Africa, exchanging instruments such as drums, lyres and flutes. The functionalist theory holds that music arose to serve practical needs of the community, such as work songs that coordinated farming or fishing, ritual music for initiation and healing ceremonies, and praise songs for leaders. Coastal Swahili music such as taarab developed later through contact with Arab and Persian traders who brought instruments like the oud and qanun, blending them with local rhythms and Kiswahili poetry.
sla_notes_illustrations: Comparing a Sukuma bugobogobo work song used while weeding with a taarab love song shows how one tradition grew from communal labour while the other grew from coastal trade and poetry.
sla_notes_daily_life: Understanding these origins helps a performer choose authentic instrumentation and style when arranging traditional music for a school cultural festival.
sla_exercise: Name one theory that explains the origin of East African music traditions.::The diffusionist theory (or the functionalist theory).||What role did Arab and Persian traders play in the origin of taarab?::They introduced instruments such as the oud and qanun that blended with local Swahili rhythms and poetry.||Give one example of a functional purpose of traditional music.::Coordinating communal work, such as songs sung while farming or fishing.

learning_activity_name: Sing extended local and foreign songs
sla_name: Singing extended local and foreign songs
sla_assessment_criteria: Extended local and foreign songs are sung correctly.
sla_teaching_aids: Piano|Guitar|Ngoma|Audio|Video clips of extended local|Foreign songs|Music scores|Music sheets
sla_references: TET(2023), MUSIC SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Extended songs are longer, multi-section pieces that demand greater breath control, dynamic range, diction and stylistic awareness than short songs.
sla_notes_details: Singers rehearse extended local pieces (such as a full traditional ngoma song with verses and a chorus) and extended foreign pieces (such as an art song or an extended choral arrangement), paying attention to breath management across long phrases, dynamic contrast between sections, clear diction in the song's language, and appropriate voice part (soprano, alto, tenor, bass) within an ensemble. Interpretation includes shaping the climax of the piece and maintaining pitch accuracy through key or tempo changes.
sla_notes_illustrations: A choir rehearses an extended arrangement of Tanzania's national anthem alongside an extended foreign piece, comparing how breath control needs differ between the two languages and styles.
sla_notes_daily_life: Church and school choirs perform extended pieces at graduations and national celebrations, where strong breath control and diction keep the audience engaged throughout.
sla_exercise: What does breath management help a singer achieve in an extended song?::It allows the singer to sustain long phrases without losing tone quality or pitch.||Name one element of interpretation important in an extended song.::Shaping the dynamic climax of the piece (or maintaining clear diction).||Give an example of an extended local song type.::A full ngoma or traditional song with several verses and a chorus.

sla_assessment_criteria: Music for pitched musical instruments are written correctly using notation software.

sla_references: TET(2023), MUSIC SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Notation software allows a musician to input, edit and print music for pitched instruments quickly and accurately compared to handwriting a score.
sla_notes_details: Using software such as MuseScore or Sibelius, students select an instrument (piano, guitar, marimba), set the correct key signature and time signature, enter notes using the mouse, keyboard shortcuts or a MIDI keyboard, and add dynamics, articulation and lyrics. The finished score can be played back to check for errors, transposed automatically for a different instrument, and exported as a PDF for printing or as a MIDI/audio file for sharing.
sla_notes_illustrations: A student enters a four-bar piano melody in C major into MuseScore, corrects a wrong note heard on playback, and exports the piece as a PDF to give to a classmate.
sla_notes_daily_life: Music teachers use notation software to prepare clean, professional-looking scores for school choirs and bands instead of copying parts by hand.
sla_exercise: Name one notation software programme used to write music for pitched instruments.::MuseScore (or Sibelius).||Why is playback useful when using notation software?::It lets the user hear the piece and catch wrong notes or rhythms before printing.||Give one format a finished score can be exported to.::PDF (or MIDI/audio file).

specific_competence_name: Play local and foreign musical instruments
learning_activity_name: Use local and foreign musical instruments (strings, percussion and wind) to accompany songs in an ensemble
sla_name: Using local and foreign instruments to accompany songs in an ensemble
sla_assessment_criteria: Song are well accompanied in an ensemble using local and foreign musical instruments.
sla_references: TET(2023), MUSIC SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: An ensemble blends local instruments such as the zeze, marimba and ngoma with foreign instruments such as the guitar, piano and violin to accompany a song.
sla_notes_details: Accompaniment can be chordal, where an instrument like the guitar or piano plays block or broken chords that support the harmony, or rhythmic, where drums and percussion provide an ostinato pattern that drives the beat. Musicians balance and blend the instruments by adjusting volume and tone so that no single instrument overpowers the singers, and they agree on a common tempo and key before performing together.
sla_notes_illustrations: In rehearsal, a guitarist plays chords for a patriotic song while a ngoma drummer keeps a steady ostinato rhythm, and the group adjusts the guitar's volume so the singers remain audible above the drum.
sla_notes_daily_life: School ensembles combining local drums with a keyboard or guitar perform this way at assemblies and cultural events throughout Tanzania.
sla_exercise: Give one example of a local instrument used in ensemble accompaniment.::Zeze, marimba, or ngoma.||What is the difference between chordal and rhythmic accompaniment?::Chordal accompaniment supports the harmony with chords, while rhythmic accompaniment provides a repeated beat pattern (ostinato).||Why must instruments be balanced in volume during an ensemble performance?::So that no instrument overpowers the singers or the other instruments.

specific_competence_name: Demonstrate an understanding of the principles of professional ethical conduct in the music industry
learning_activity_name: Discuss the ethics, norms and values governing the music industry in Tanzania (things that are acceptable, and tolerable against the things that are taboo).
sla_name: Ethics, norms and values in the music industry
sla_assessment_criteria: Ethics, norms and values governing the music industry in Tanzania are well discussed.
sla_teaching_aids: BASATA|COSOTA guidelines|Audio/ video clips of Tanzanian music
sla_references: TET(2023), MUSIC SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: The Tanzanian music industry is guided by ethical standards, norms and values that determine what is acceptable, tolerable or taboo in musical content and business practice.
sla_notes_details: Professional conduct includes respecting copyright by registering works with COSOTA and not pirating other artists' work, following content classification and decency guidelines set by BASATA, honouring contracts with producers and promoters, and avoiding plagiarism. Norms and values also cover on-stage conduct, appropriate lyrical content for different audiences, and fair treatment of band members and collaborators in payment and credit.
sla_notes_illustrations: A songwriter registers a new song with COSOTA before releasing it, ensuring royalties are collected whenever the song is played on radio or streamed.
sla_notes_daily_life: Artists who follow these ethics build a trustworthy reputation and avoid legal disputes over royalties or copied material, which is common in the local music business.
sla_exercise: What does COSOTA protect for a musician?::Copyright, so the artist can collect royalties when the work is used.||Name the body that sets content classification guidelines for the arts in Tanzania.::BASATA.||Give one example of unethical conduct in the music industry.::Plagiarism (or piracy of another artist's work).

sla_assessment_criteria: Different song productions are mixed successfully using ICT.
sla_teaching_aids: A computer installed with DAW|MIDI controller|Sound card|Studio microphone|Studio monitors
sla_references: TET(2023), MUSIC SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Mixing is the stage of music production where individual recorded tracks are balanced and processed to create one polished stereo recording.
sla_notes_details: Using a Digital Audio Workstation (DAW), the engineer sets the level (volume) of each track, pans instruments and voices across the stereo field, applies equalisation (EQ) to shape the tone of each track, uses compression to control dynamic range, and adds effects such as reverb or delay for depth. The tracks are then bounced down into a single stereo mix file.
sla_notes_illustrations: A student mixes a recorded song by lowering the level of a boomy bass guitar, panning backing vocals slightly left and right, and adding light reverb to the lead vocal before exporting the final mix.
sla_notes_daily_life: Home studio producers and church sound teams use these same mixing steps to prepare recordings for radio play or online release.
sla_exercise: What is the purpose of equalisation (EQ) in mixing?::To shape the tone of a track by boosting or cutting certain frequencies.||Why is panning used in a mix?::To place instruments and voices at different positions across the stereo field for clarity and space.||Name one software tool used for mixing songs.::A Digital Audio Workstation (DAW).

specific_competence_name: Use ICT to produce and master music
learning_activity_name: Perform the mastering (finishing) of different song productions using ICT
sla_assessment_criteria: Different song productions are mastered successfully using ICT.
sla_teaching_aids: Music scores|Music sheets|Piano|Guitar|Electronic device with notation software
sla_references: TET(2023), MUSIC SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Mastering is the final stage of production that prepares a finished mix for distribution by ensuring consistent loudness and tonal balance.
sla_notes_details: During mastering, the engineer applies gentle overall EQ to balance tone across the whole track, uses a limiter to raise the loudness to a competitive level without distortion, checks the mix in mono and on different playback systems, and exports the final file in formats suitable for distribution such as WAV for quality and MP3 for streaming. When mastering an album or EP, tracks are also matched in loudness and tone so the whole collection sounds consistent.
sla_notes_illustrations: A student masters a finished mix by applying a limiter to raise its loudness to match commercial releases, then exports both a WAV master and an MP3 copy for online distribution.
sla_notes_daily_life: Independent artists master their own songs this way before uploading them to streaming platforms so the tracks sound professional next to major-label releases.
sla_exercise: What is the main purpose of mastering?::To ensure the final track has consistent loudness and tonal balance ready for distribution.||Name one tool commonly used at the mastering stage.::A limiter.||Why should tracks on the same album be matched in loudness during mastering?::So the whole collection sounds consistent when played back to back.

specific_competence_name: Design and conduct a project in music
learning_activity_name: Design and carry out a project in music
sla_name: Designing and carrying out a project in music
sla_assessment_criteria: A project in music is designed and carried out successfully.
sla_teaching_aids: Videos related to successful music business ventures|Industry reports|Market research
sla_references: TET(2023), MUSIC SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: A music project lets a student apply composition, performance, production or business skills to a real, self-directed piece of work.
sla_notes_details: The design stage requires choosing a clear objective (for example, composing an original song, running a small recording session, or a music business venture), stating the methodology and steps to be followed, listing the resources and instruments needed, and setting a realistic timeline. Students then begin executing the first phase of the project, such as writing the song's melody and lyrics or drafting a business plan, keeping records of decisions and progress for later reporting.
sla_notes_illustrations: A student designs a project to compose and record an original patriotic song, planning two weeks for songwriting, one week for rehearsal and one week for recording, then begins writing the lyrics and melody.
sla_notes_daily_life: This project process mirrors how professional musicians and small music businesses plan an album or event from idea to execution.
sla_exercise: What should a music project's design stage include?::A clear objective, methodology, required resources and a timeline.||Give an example of a music project objective.::Composing and recording an original song (or starting a small music business venture).||Why is it important to keep records of decisions during the project?::So progress can be tracked and reported accurately when the project is reviewed.

learning_activity_name: Describe the fundamentals of reading and writing music based on ABRSM Music Theory Grade VI (Rhythm, and melody and harmony)
sla_name: Fundamentals of reading and writing music (Grade VI)
sla_assessment_criteria: Fundamentals of reading and writing music based on ABRSM Music Theory Grade VI are explained correctly.
sla_teaching_aids: ABRSM music theory guideline|Music scores|Music sheets|Piano|Guitar|Ngoma
sla_references: TET(2023), MUSIC SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: ABRSM Grade VI theory extends Grade V knowledge with more advanced scales, ornamentation and score analysis skills.
sla_notes_details: At this level, students work with scales and key signatures up to six sharps and six flats, recognise and use ornaments such as grace notes, trills and turns, understand transposing instruments in general terms (for example a Bb clarinet sounding a tone lower than written), and study basic figured bass symbols. Students also learn to detect and correct errors in a given musical excerpt, such as a wrong note, incorrect rhythm or missing accidental.
sla_notes_illustrations: Given a printed melody with a deliberately wrong note under a G major key signature, a student identifies the note that does not belong to the scale and corrects it.
sla_notes_daily_life: Music examiners and arrangers use this same error-spotting skill to proofread scores before they are printed or performed.
sla_exercise: What is an ornament in music? Give an example.::A decorative addition to a melody, such as a grace note, trill or turn.||What happens to the sounding pitch of a Bb clarinet compared to the written note?::It sounds a tone (whole step) lower than written.||Name one skill developed through Grade VI theory error-detection exercises.::Identifying a wrong note, rhythm or missing accidental in a score.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of some advanced theories and principles of music
specific_competence_name: Demonstrate an understanding of some advanced theories of music
learning_activity_name: Describe the theories related to origins of different music traditions in Africa
sla_name: Origins of music traditions in Africa
sla_assessment_criteria: Theories related to origins of different music traditions in Africa are explained correctly.
sla_teaching_aids: Audio|Video clips of various African traditional ensemble performances
sla_references: TET(2023), MUSIC SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Beyond East Africa, music traditions across West, Central and Southern Africa also have distinct historical origins shaped by oral tradition, migration and communal life.
sla_notes_details: West African music traditions are closely tied to the griot system, hereditary oral historians and musicians who preserved history, genealogy and praise songs through generations using instruments such as the kora and balafon. Central African traditions, such as those of the mbira among the Shona people, developed from spiritual and ceremonial practice linking the living with ancestors. Southern African traditions show call-and-response patterns rooted in communal labour and storytelling. Comparing these theories with East African ones highlights common threads of oral transmission and community function across the continent.
sla_notes_illustrations: The mbira tradition of the Shona people in Zimbabwe is compared with the taarab tradition of the Swahili coast to show how one grew from ancestral ceremony and the other from coastal trade.
sla_notes_daily_life: Understanding these varied origins helps a performer explain and respect the cultural background of a piece before performing or arranging it for an audience.
sla_exercise: What role did griots play in West African music tradition?::They were hereditary oral historians and musicians who preserved history and praise songs through music.||Name an instrument associated with the mbira tradition's origin.::The mbira (thumb piano) itself.||Give one common thread shared by African music traditions from different regions.::Oral transmission of history and culture through music (or a strong communal function).

sla_assessment_criteria: Various song compositions are transposed correctly.
sla_references: TET(2023), MUSIC SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Transposition means rewriting a piece of music in a different key while keeping the same melodic and harmonic relationships.
sla_notes_details: To transpose, a musician chooses the target key, works out the interval between the old and new key (for example, transposing up a major second), and shifts every note by that same interval while adjusting the key signature accordingly. For transposing instruments such as the Bb trumpet or clarinet, the written part must sound a specific interval different from the actual pitch, so the arranger writes the part a tone higher (for Bb instruments) than the sounding pitch.
sla_notes_illustrations: A song written in C major is transposed to D major (up a major second) so a vocalist with a higher range can sing it comfortably, with every note and the key signature adjusted accordingly.
sla_notes_daily_life: Choir directors transpose hymns and songs like this every week to fit the vocal range of whichever singers are available.
sla_exercise: What does transposition mean in music?::Rewriting a piece in a different key while keeping the same melodic and harmonic relationships.||Why might a song be transposed for a singer?::To fit the song comfortably within that singer's vocal range.||How is a part written for a Bb trumpet different from the sounding pitch?::It is written a tone higher than the actual sounding pitch.

sla_name: Modulating songs composed in various languages
sla_assessment_criteria: Songs composed in various languages are modulated correctly.
sla_teaching_aids: Music scores|Music sheets|Piano|Guitar|Electronic device with notation software
sla_references: TET(2023), MUSIC SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Modulation is the process of changing from one key to another within the same piece of music to create variety or build tension.
sla_notes_details: Common modulation techniques include pivot chord modulation, where a chord shared by both keys smoothly links them, direct modulation, where the new key begins abruptly without preparation, and modulating to closely related keys such as the dominant, subdominant or relative minor, which sound natural to the ear. Composers apply the same modulation techniques whether the song's lyrics are in Kiswahili, English or another language, since modulation is a feature of the musical structure rather than the language.
sla_notes_illustrations: A song in C major modulates to G major (the dominant key) for its final chorus using a pivot chord (G major, common to both keys) to make the key change sound smooth.
sla_notes_daily_life: Composers use modulation to lift the final chorus of a song to a higher, more exciting key, a technique heard often in gospel and pop songs on the radio.
sla_exercise: What is modulation in music?::Changing from one key to another within the same piece.||Name one type of modulation.::Pivot chord modulation (or direct modulation).||Which related keys are commonly used for a smooth modulation?::The dominant, the subdominant, or the relative minor.

sla_assessment_criteria: Various song compositions are transcribed correctly.
sla_teaching_aids: Music scores|Music sheets|Piano|Guitar|Electronic device with notation software
sla_references: TET(2023), MUSIC SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Transcription is the skill of listening to a recorded song and writing out its melody, rhythm and chords in notation.
sla_notes_details: The transcriber listens repeatedly to a short section of the recording, first identifying the rhythm and time signature, then working out the melody note by note using solfa or staff notation, and finally identifying the underlying chords by ear. Slowing down playback and isolating instruments helps with accuracy, and the finished transcription is checked by playing it back against the original recording.
sla_notes_illustrations: A student transcribes the chorus of a recorded local song, first tapping out its rhythm, then finding each melody note on a keyboard, and finally writing the chord symbols above the staff.
sla_notes_daily_life: Music teachers transcribe traditional songs passed down orally so they can be preserved in written notation for future generations of students.
sla_exercise: What is transcription in music?::Writing out the melody, rhythm and chords of a recorded song in notation.||What should a transcriber identify first when transcribing a recording?::The rhythm and time signature.||How can a transcriber check the accuracy of a finished transcription?::By playing it back and comparing it with the original recording.

learning_activity_name: Sing various multi-part songs using relevant techniques
sla_name: Singing multi-part songs using relevant techniques
sla_assessment_criteria: Multi-part songs using relevant techniques are sung correctly.
sla_teaching_aids: Videos/audios of multi-part harmony songs|Piano|Guitar|Music scores|Music sheets
sla_references: TET(2023), MUSIC SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Multi-part singing requires each voice part to blend with the others while maintaining its own independent melodic line.
sla_notes_details: Techniques for multi-part singing (such as SATB harmony) include sectional rehearsal, where each voice part learns its line separately before combining, humming warm-ups to develop blend and tone matching, listening across parts to stay in tune with the harmony rather than only one's own line, and balancing volume so no single part dominates. Conductors often use hand cues to bring parts in and out and to control dynamics during a multi-part performance.
sla_notes_illustrations: A choir rehearses a four-part arrangement by first teaching the alto line alone, then the tenor line, before combining all four parts and adjusting balance so the melody in the soprano line is still heard clearly.
sla_notes_daily_life: School and church choirs use these same sectional rehearsal techniques every week to prepare multi-part hymns and anthems for services.
sla_exercise: Name one technique used to prepare a multi-part song.::Sectional rehearsal (or humming warm-ups).||Why must singers listen across parts during multi-part singing?::To stay in tune with the overall harmony rather than only their own line.||What is SATB harmony?::Four-part harmony sung by soprano, alto, tenor and bass voices.

sla_assessment_criteria: Music for unpitched musical instruments are written correctly using notation software.
sla_teaching_aids: Electronic device installed with a notation software|Piano|Guitar|Ngoma|Music scores|Music sheets
sla_references: TET(2023), MUSIC SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Unpitched percussion instruments are notated differently from pitched instruments because they show rhythm rather than exact pitch.
sla_notes_details: In notation software, unpitched percussion parts are usually written on a single-line staff or a percussion clef, with different noteheads (such as an x notehead for a hi-hat or shaker) representing different instruments. Students assign each instrument to a line or notehead shape, enter the rhythmic pattern, and can map the parts to General MIDI percussion sounds so the software plays them back realistically.
sla_notes_illustrations: A student writes a ngoma drum pattern in MuseScore using a percussion staff, assigning the low drum to one line and the high drum to another, then plays it back using mapped MIDI percussion sounds.
sla_notes_daily_life: Sound engineers and band directors use percussion notation like this to write out drum-kit or traditional-drum parts for a band to rehearse from.
sla_exercise: Why are unpitched instruments notated differently from pitched instruments?::Because they represent rhythm rather than exact pitch, so they use a single-line or percussion staff instead of a normal pitched staff.||What is used in notation software to represent different unpitched instruments?::Different notehead shapes (such as an x notehead) on assigned lines.||What can a percussion part be mapped to for realistic playback?::General MIDI percussion sounds.

sla_name: Using local and foreign instruments to accompany contemporary songs in an ensemble
sla_assessment_criteria: Local and foreign musical instruments are used correctly to accompany contemporary songs in an ensemble.
sla_references: TET(2023), MUSIC SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Contemporary ensembles blend local instruments such as the baragumu and filimbi with foreign instruments such as the saxophone, trumpet, guitar and piano to accompany modern songs.
sla_notes_details: In a contemporary arrangement (such as bongo fleva or Afrobeat-style music), the guitar and piano typically provide the chordal backbone, brass instruments like the saxophone and trumpet add melodic riffs or punctuating stabs, and local wind instruments like the filimbi or the baragumu are woven in for a distinctive local colour or fanfare effect. Musicians rehearse to match tempo, dynamics and style so the mix of local and foreign instruments sounds unified rather than two separate groups playing at once.
sla_notes_illustrations: In rehearsal, a guitar and piano play the chord progression of a contemporary song while a saxophone adds a short melodic riff between vocal lines and a filimbi plays a brief local-flavoured introduction.
sla_notes_daily_life: Popular Tanzanian bands regularly mix instruments this way to give their contemporary songs both an international sound and a recognisable local identity.
sla_exercise: Give one example of a local instrument used in a contemporary ensemble.::Baragumu (or filimbi).||What role do the guitar and piano typically play in a contemporary arrangement?::They provide the chordal backbone of the song.||Why do musicians rehearse to match tempo and style across local and foreign instruments?::So the combined sound feels unified rather than like two separate groups playing at once.

sla_notes_intro: The Form Six project continues the project designed and started in Form Five, ending with a completed report on its outcomes.
sla_notes_details: Completing the project involves finishing the planned activities, such as the final recording, performance or business venture, then writing a report that evaluates whether the original objectives were achieved, records the challenges faced (such as limited equipment or scheduling conflicts) and how they were solved, and gives recommendations for anyone continuing similar work. The finished report and any accompanying recording or product are submitted for assessment, sometimes with an oral presentation defending the work.
sla_notes_illustrations: A student who began recording an original song in Form Five completes the mixing and mastering in Form Six, then writes a report describing how a shortage of studio time was solved by recording in shorter, focused sessions.
sla_notes_daily_life: Professional music producers likewise document and evaluate their projects this way when applying for funding or presenting results to a record label.
